Rashi on Nedarim 40a:11:1.hebrew: סהדא רבה פרת - כשנהר פרת גדול, הוי עדות לגשמים שיורדין לא"י, דא"י גבוה מכל הארצות, ובאין גשמים ונופלין בפרת ומתגדל מהן. והאי דאמרי' דנהר מתגדל ממי הגשמים, הוי פלוגתא אדשמואל:
Rashi on Nedarim 40a:11:1.english: A great witness [is] the Euphrates - When the Euphrates River is swollen, it is testimony to rains that fall in Eretz Yisrael, for Eretz Yisrael is higher than all [other] lands, and the rains come and fall into the Euphrates and it grows from them. And this that we say, that a river grows from rainwater, is a dispute with Shmuel.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:11:2.english: A river is blessed from its banks - For it wells up from its banks, and not from rainwater.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:1:1.english: Ba'ish - He fell ill, and there are those who have the reading "ba'ash".

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:1:2.english: As though he is spilling blood - Because people who enter to visit him attend to all of the sick person's needs.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:2:1.english: Neither that he will live nor that he will die - For he does not know the condition of the sick person.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:3:1.hebrew: דלא ליתרע מזליה - דדילמא מתצלנא לאלתר, אי נמי דלא לישתעי מילי עילויה:
Rashi on Nedarim 40a:3:1.english: So that his luck not suffer - For perhaps I will recover immediately; or else, so that [people] not speak words about him.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:3:2.hebrew: מכאן ואילך - חזי דלא מתרפא, אמר להו: פוקו ואכריזו:
Rashi on Nedarim 40a:3:2.english: From this [point] forward - [Since] he saw that he was not recovering, he said to them: Go out and proclaim.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:6:1.hebrew: ריעים כנעמן - שריפאוהו מצרעתו, כגון אלישע דהוה נביא וזקן, והשיאו עצה לנעמן:
Rashi on Nedarim 40a:6:1.english: Companions like Naaman - Who healed him of his leprosy, such as Elisha, who was a prophet and an elder, and they gave counsel to Naaman.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:7:1.english: If youths say to you: Build - the Temple.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:7:2.english: And elders say, "Demolish" - and do not build.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:7:3.hebrew: וסימן לדבר מרחבעם - דכתיב (מלכים א י״ב:ח׳) ויעזוב את עצת הזקנים וגו', ונחרב בית המקדש על אותה עצה. והמורה לא פירש בבית המקדש, ואיכא ברייתא דקתני בהדיא בבית המקדש:
Rashi on Nedarim 40a:7:3.english: And a mnemonic for the matter [is] from Rehoboam - For it is written (I Kings 12:8): "But he forsook the counsel of the elders," etc., and the Temple was destroyed on account of that counsel. And the teacher did not explain [that it refers to] the Temple, yet there is a baraita that explicitly teaches [that it refers to] the Temple.

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:8:1.english: Not to visit [לסעוד] - As in (Numbers 16:29), "and the visitation of [ופקודת] all men," [which] we translate [into Aramaic as] "vese'uda" [וסעודא].

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:8:2.hebrew: תלת שעי קמייתא רווחא דעתיה - כדאמר בעלמא (ב"ב טז:) אידלי יומא אידלי קצירא, ודילמא אמר: לא אצטריך למבעי רחמי עליה, דאינו כל כך חולה:
Rashi on Nedarim 40a:8:2.english: [During] the first three hours his mind is relieved - As it says elsewhere (Bava Batra 16b): "[When] the day rises, the sick person is relieved," and perhaps [the visitor] will say, "It is not necessary to pray for mercy for him, for he is not so sick."

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:9:1.english: [He] will sustain him - Like [the verse], "and bread sustains the heart of man" (Psalms 104:15).

Rashi on Nedarim 40a:9:2.hebrew: ומניין שהשכינה כו' שנאמר ה' יסעדנו - קרי ביה יסערנו, אי כמי יסעדנו ממש, שמסעד שכינה על ראשו, כדאמרן בהדיא ששכינה שרויה למעלה ממיטתו:
Rashi on Nedarim 40a:9:2.english: And from where [is it derived] that the Divine Presence, etc., as it is stated, “The Lord will support him” - Read into it yisa'arenu [hovering over him]; or alternatively, yis'adenu literally, for He rests [His] Divine Presence over his head, as we said explicitly, that the Divine Presence rests above his bed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 40a:11:1.english: A great witness is the Euphrates - [meaning] that its waters have increased from the rains.

Tosafot on Nedarim 40a:8:1.english: Lis'od [to visit] - [This means] if he visits a sick person. We translate [the Hebrew word] poked [into Aramaic] as vesa'ed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 40a:8:2.hebrew: רווח נפשיה - החולה, וסבור המבקר שהחולה עובר לו חליו, ונמנע מלבקש רחמים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 40a:8:2.english: He feels relieved - [That is,] the sick person; and the visitor thinks [that] the sick person's illness is passing from him, and he refrains from praying for mercy.

Tosafot on Nedarim 40a:8:3.english: In the last three [hours], his weakness intensifies - and [the visitor] is diverted from praying for mercy for him.
